DS_e973eadd57.displayName: Heat shock response in sensitive mutants (LRR5, DHC)
DS_e973eadd57.description:
General Description: To determine genes that may underlie the HS-response, HS-Sensitive mutants were compared to wild-type. Two individual HS-Sensitive mutant clonal lines were profiled via RNAseq to identify dysregulated genes responsible for this sensitivity: ΔDHC and ΔLRR5 (dynein heavy-chain gene PF3D7_1122900 and leucine-rich repeat protein PF3D7_1432400)

Methodology used: Synchronized cultures of wild-type NF54 and HS-Sensitive mutants ΔDHC and ΔLRR5 were grown at normal human body temperature (37℃) or cycled three times at 41℃. After the third round of heat shock, RNA was harvested simultaneously from both conditions for RNAseq. RNAseq was performed on an Illumina MiSeq using a 300-cycle V2 MiSeq reagent kit.

DS_24d441b301.displayName: Protein targets of serum antibodies in response to infection
DS_24d441b301.description: Plasma collected from human subjects before and after the 6-month Mali malaria season (220 individuals) was hybridized to protein microarrays containing ~23% of the P. falciparum proteome, negative and positive controls and an IgG standard curve. Antibody binding to the protein microarray was detected by streptavidin-conjugated SureLight P-3. Antibody profiles for each patient were generated and significant differential antibody reactivity was calculated.
